source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Νικηφόρος ο Πρεσβύτερος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and then says that it is unknown in what age he lived. **The display name carries the day and not the epithet**: the calendar calls him ο Πρεσβύτερος, which `types` would repeat, and the page's own account makes him abbot of a monastery, so «of Ephapsis» would be a name saint.gr never gives him. **No year of any kind, so no `dates` object.** **He is none of the corpus's fifteen Nicephori**, which the namesweep flagged and which were read; none of them is the abbot of Ephapsis and none is kept on 13 May. **The dupscan's one near-slug is answered here**: `nicephorus-4-may` is a bare Romanian line, «Sfantul Cuvios Nichifor» on 4 mai, with no life, no century, no country and no monastery, so nothing about him can be matched against this one except the name — and the days are nine apart, which is neither the same day nor a style conversion. Drafted as another man on the standing rule that a name alone is never a match; if the writer judges otherwise, this is the folder of the day to turn into an upgrade. **The page names a companion the corpus cannot hold**: «Ορισμένοι Συναξαριστές μαζί του, αναφέρουν και τη μνήμη κάποιου Οσίου Αγαπίου» — some synaxaria commemorate a venerable Agapios with him — and that is all it says of the man, so no folder is made for him and he is named in the life without a link.
